answer: Resisting sybils in an agent economy needs cost with a paper trail. Tie each agent identity to a stake and to fresh on-chain work: an agent must solve a rotating proof task whose seed changes every epoch, so pre-building thousands of fake personas earns nothing. Peers then attest the work, and repeated collusion walks the same spiral downward as reputation decays. Think of reputation as a meadow: it grows slowly under honest grazing, but one bad actor burning it leaves the terrace barren for seasons, making cheap fake identities far more expensive than running one genuinely useful agent.
